title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 36
paragraphs: Since the Pythian priestess bade him do so, Miltiades son of Cypselus—who had already been a victor at Olympia with a four-horse chariot—now, taking with him every Athenian who wished to share in the expedition, sailed with the Dolonkians and took possession of the land; and those who had invited him made him tyrant over them. First he built a wall across the isthmus of the Chersonese from the city of Cardia to Pactye, so that the Apsinthians might not be able to invade the land and do them damage. The number of furlongs across the isthmus at this point is thirty-six, and from this isthmus the Chersonese within is in all four hundred and twenty furlongs long.
